mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face higher costs.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE falls below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past 3 months signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of instances where INDPRO declines by more than 2% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals a potential overheating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% and CPIAUCSL is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 2% over 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 2% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from increased consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases over a 3-month period.
